featured_reviews.name: Mayur
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Golden Wave Restaurant in Santacruz, Mumbai, for dinner with family and friends. The restaurant has a pleasant ambience with comfortable seating and a relaxed atmosphere, making it a good place for an evening meal.

We started our dinner with the Chicken Tandoori, which was well-marinated, nicely cooked, and packed with authentic smoky flavors. The chicken was tender and served fresh, making it the highlight of our meal. For the main course, we ordered the Mutton Dum Biryani. The biryani had aromatic rice and flavorful spices, while the mutton was cooked well and complemented the dish nicely.

However, the overall dining experience was affected by a couple of drawbacks. The service was noticeably slow, and we had to wait longer than expected for our food to arrive. While the quality and taste of the dishes were satisfactory, the portion sizes felt quite small considering the prices charged. This made the meal seem less value-for-money than we had anticipated.

That said, the restaurant's ambience and the taste of the food were enjoyable enough to make the visit worthwhile. If the management improves the speed of service and offers more generous portions, the overall experience would be significantly better.

Overall, Golden Wave Restaurant offers decent food in a pleasant setting, but there is room for improvement in service efficiency and portion sizes. I would rate my experience 3 out of 5 stars.

featured_reviews.name: Swapnil Utekar
featured_reviews.review_text:
The ambiance of the restaurant is really good and creates a pleasant dining atmosphere. However, the food experience was average considering the price range.
The service was decent and staff were polite, but a couple of dishes didn’t meet expectations. The Chicken Chilly and Achari Paneer Masala were noticeably more salty than usual. The Achari Paneer lacked the expected tangy flavour and tasted saltier instead.
That said, the food was not bad overall. The Chicken Tikka, Veg Spring Rolls, and Masala Soda were quite good and enjoyable.
Overall, it was an average dining experience compared to what I was expecting. The place has great ambiance and potential, but some improvement in taste balance and consistency would make the experience much better.

Whether you’re planning a date night, a family dinner, or even dining solo, this place offers the perfect ambiance. Highly recommended I’ll definitely be coming back again! ✨

featured_reviews.name: Ramsha Tausalkar
featured_reviews.review_text: There’s a new South Indian food spot in the city so I had to check it out. Nanna House in Bandra is serving Andhra style food and I tried their specials. The Karam Podi Dosa is your usual slick dosa, but with Karam Podi masala which was too spicy for me. The Pesarattu, a healthy moong dal dosa, was perfect though. I really enjoyed it. Another of their healthy offerings is the Millet Cone Idli, served in this very cute manner. It is plain and pasty, and a must try. All of this comes with 4 chutneys, each with their own kick. What you can’t miss here at all is their Filter Kaapi Soft Serve - it’s like creamy cold coffee. So good. Overall, this place offers unique and healthy options, so if that’s what you like, check it out.

featured_reviews.name: sucheta thakur
featured_reviews.review_text:
If there’s one place Bandra needs to start forming lines for, it’s @nannahouseindia on 16th Road. This Andhra-style spot is all set to change the way Bandra — actually, Bombay — experiences South Indian food. And yes, maybe it sounds like I’m exaggerating… but one meal here is enough to prove why I’m not.

From the moment the food arrived, everything reminded me of the kind of flavours that feel simple, comforting, yet absolutely unforgettable.

We started with the Pesarattu, beautifully stuffed with upma — a combination that instantly transported me back to Hyderabad. The texture, the seasoning, the warmth… it just hits in the most nostalgic way.

Next up was the star of the show: the Butter Masala Dosa. Cooked in Amul butter and finished with a generous dollop of white butter, this dosa is easily one of the best in Bombay. Crisp edges, a soft centre, flavour-packed masala — truly dosa heaven.

The Butter Podi Idli followed the same theme — soft idlis coated in podi and topped with white butter. Comforting, buttery, and delicious in every bite.

And of course, no South Indian meal is complete without Filter Coffee. Their version is strong, aromatic, and balanced — exactly how a proper filter coffee should be.

But the surprise winner? The Filter Coffee Soft Serve. Smooth, perfectly sweet, full of coffee flavour — honestly, the perfect end to this meal. I’d go back just for this. ❤️

In a city overflowing with restaurants, Nanna House India stands out for its authenticity, warmth, and flavour-packed dishes. What are you waiting for? This is the place Bandra needs queues for — and trust me, once you try it, you’ll understand why.

featured_reviews.name: Vardhita Parekh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Overall, the experience was okay, but they definitely need to work on their management. It was quite crowded, and the person handling it wasn’t able to manage things well. Plus, the kiosk machine for ordering and payment wasn’t working, which made it a bit inconvenient.
Food Feedback:
1) Karam Podi Dosa – Felt dry and was served cold.
2) Ghee Podi Idli – Hardly any podi, and the idli was way too soft — almost like it wasn’t cooked properly.
3) Millet Cone Idli – Nice and different, but they can totally skip the ice-cream stick.

5) Chutney – Would be great if they could increase the quantity a bit.

featured_reviews.name: Kinjal Jethwa
featured_reviews.review_text:
I am so in love with Andhra cuisine — those soft, soft idlis and dosas are my absolute weakness! I recently visited a new place that opened in Bandra, and it’s perfect for breakfast, lunch, or dinner.
The food here is pure bliss. The chutney, the sambhar — the authenticity is just amazing. The millet cone idli was my favourite!
We also tried their Ghee Podi Idli and Button Vada — so fresh and so yummy, I just couldn’t say no.
The Karam Masala Dosa was nice and crispy, and the Poori Saagu was absolutely ultimate.
Overall, the food is superb and I truly enjoyed every bit of it.
And lastly… Filter Coffee is a must before you wrap up your meal.
Do check this place out if you’re an idli fan just like me!
They have limited menu but super tasty 🤤

featured_reviews.name: Farhan Shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you are searching for authentic Andhra food in Bandra, Nanna House is a place you should not miss. This South Indian cafe specialises in traditional Andhra cuisine, and the flavours truly reflect home-style cooking. The millet cone idlis were soft and wholesome, and the podi idlis had the perfect balance of ghee and spice.

The dosa selection is excellent. The karam podi dosa was spicy, crisp, and full of flavour, while the butter masala dosa was comforting and indulgent. Every dish felt freshly prepared and true to South Indian food traditions, making it one of the better South Indian restaurants in Bandra.

The highlight for me was the putharekulu dessert, a rare Andhra sweet that is difficult to find in Mumbai. Light, ghee-rich, and delicately sweet, it ended the meal beautifully. Add a cup of traditional filter coffee and the experience feels complete. Highly recommended for anyone looking for the best Andhra restaurant in Bandra.

featured_reviews.name: Mommy OnDuty
featured_reviews.review_text: Nice cozy ambience with awesome south indian food. All dishes tastes delicious and is priced appropriate for the pocket. Dont forget to try its Karam podi dosa, andhra style poori sagu, ghee dosa with authentic filter coffee….

featured_reviews.name: 1TeaspoonLove
featured_reviews.review_text:

The dishes are served with 4 types of chutneys and sambar.

The idlis were super soft almost melted in the mouth. We loved the Babai idli which were dipped in ghee topped with white butter. So good! The podi idli was good too.

We tried the Karam podi and pesarattu .. both were crisp and tasted good. The karam podi was garlicky and spicy.

We also tried the cone ragi idli which were decent.

The filter coffee was good but the filter coffee soft serve was excellent. Must try. It was smooth creamy and perfect.

Overall good food.

featured_reviews.name: Shadab Qureshi
featured_reviews.review_text:
**“Extremely disappointing and mentally frustrating experience. I ordered 2 Masala Dosa and 2 boxes of Medu Wada (each box containing 4 pieces, around ₹211 each), along with a watermelon juice add-on.

Shockingly, I did not receive the Medu Wada at all. I only received 2 boxes containing Masala Dosa with chutney and sambhar.

When I contacted the restaurant, they first told me to check properly and said there should be 3 boxes. After confirming with their kitchen, they firmly stated that everything was packed and sent correctly. Then they shifted the responsibility, saying if anything happens during transit, it is Zomato and the delivery partner’s issue.

But this is where the real problem lies. Instead of taking accountability or properly investigating, responsibility is being passed around. This creates a system where no one is answerable, and the only person who suffers is the customer who paid honestly.

Also, blaming the delivery stage so casually makes no sense. A delivery partner is not just a middle person—they are the backbone of this entire system. Without them, restaurants cannot deliver food and platforms cannot function. Indirectly shifting blame without clarity or resolution only reflects poor coordination and lack of accountability in the entire process.

In the end, both the restaurant and Zomato get paid, but the customer is left with incomplete food, no proper explanation, no immediate support, and only different excuses from everyone involved.

This is not just about a missing item, it reflects a deeper issue of responsibility, coordination, and customer respect. Very irresponsible service and a truly disappointing experience.”**

“If the system cannot ensure accountability, then the customer will always be the weakest and most ignored part of it.”

Beeji ki Rasoi is special for every kid, so when I saw there is a delivery kitchen named after one - I couldn’t resist & ordered some food last night to try it out.

For people who don’t know :- Beeji in punjabi means mom or grand mother.

My Veg Order was as follows :-
Veg Kadhai Dhaba
* Veg Kadhai subzi - Tasty
* Chole Masala subzi - Delicious
* Dal Makhani - Simply irresistible
* Steam Rice - Perfectly Cooked
* Sheera ( dessert ) - My favourite
* Chapati ( 4 of them ) - Soft

Note :- All Dhaba’s contain 4 chapatis, Bhaji, Black Dal, Rice, Meetha, Salad, Onion, Sprout & Pickle.

Cheese Chilli Paratha
The cheese & chilli stuffing was spicy & pretty heavy so order accordingly.
It blended beautifully with Chole &
Dal Makhani. I personally prefer Paratha / Naan over chapati or Rotis with my
North Indian Curries.

Beeji ki Rasoi lives up to its famous tag line & offers Customised packaging, great food quality & decent quantity ensuring our order is sufficient for 2 eaters.
If you don’t stay with your beeji or family members - after eating from beeji ki Rasoi you’ll definitely remember your family 😍

Aloo paratha

Four huge pieces of aloo paratha with heavenly stuffing comes with onion and pickle. Loved the aloo masala was really flavourful ... Loved it.

Nanumal Bhojraj in Santacruz is an absolute culinary gem, a testament to how simple, home-style food can truly shine. Despite arriving well past 10:15 PM, the warm reception was immediate – no hint of hesitation, just genuine hospitality. The staff were incredibly accommodating, offering excellent suggestions that proved to be spot-on.
The Dal Khichdi was a revelation; comforting, flavorful, and reminiscent of the best homemade versions. It was simple yet profoundly satisfying, a true highlight. The Schezwan Noodles were equally impressive, striking the perfect balance of spice and tang, each strand cooked to perfection. featured_reviews.name: Benjamin SHIH
featured_reviews.review_text:
This is my first time visiting India, and I’m so glad we found this gem. The Owner/Chef is incredibly welcoming; he personally helped us order and explained the flavors with such passion.
We are from Taiwan and have tried many top-tier Indian restaurants back home, like Saffron (番紅花), Taj (泰姬), and Mayur (馬友友). But the Gosht Lucknowi Dum Biryani here is on a whole different level. My friend even said it’s 10 times better!
• The Mutton: I’ve never had mutton this tender. It’s perfectly marinated and practically falls apart. You can really taste the "Kung Fu" the Chef puts into the slow-cooking.
• The Sauce: That rich, golden gravy isn't just a sauce; it's a concentration of slow-cooked onions and spices that melt in your mouth.
• The Pro Move: Make sure to mix in the spicy yogurt raita. It cuts through the richness and adds a whole new layer of flavor to the fragrant rice.
If you want a meal made with genuine heart and soul, this is the place. A huge thank you to the Chef for such a warm welcome to India!

featured_reviews.name: Shreeya Mehrotra
featured_reviews.review_text:
I’m a North Indian living in Mumbai, and everyone knows that Mumbai doesn’t really do good North Indian food unless it’s fancy. Most days you just adjust, but some days you really miss proper food. That’s exactly the kind of day I found Bombay Curry and honestly I’m so glad I did. This place feels so homely. It’s the kind of place you go to on a random night when you’ve had a bad day, you’re tired and you just want something that feels like home.

We ordered butter chicken, garlic naan and seekh kebab and every single thing was a straight 10/10. The butter chicken was rich and comforting, the garlic naan was soft and perfect and the seekh kebabs were juicy and full of flavour.

What makes it even more special is knowing that the chefs are from Lucknow and Rajasthan because you can genuinely taste that authenticity in the food. And the chef/owner himself was easily one of the most friendly and nicest chefs I’ve ever met. Warm, welcoming and clearly cooking with a lot of love. Bombay Curry feels like a hug on a plate.

featured_reviews.name: Sagar “Sagar Anil” A
featured_reviews.review_text:
Our experience was an 80–20 mix, but overall quite memorable. We’ve visited multiple restaurants across Mumbai and often seen chefs deeply occupied with their cooking schedules. Here, however, we met Chef Kunal Nagpal—a chef with a story, beautifully balancing restaurant management and creating magic with his food.

We reached the hotel around 3:45 PM, just before closing time, which meant our order was taken in a bit of a hurry. We patiently waited for the food, and that’s where the experience truly took a turn for the better.

We ordered Chicken Malai Tikka and Butter Chicken, and both dishes were outstanding. The masala was rich and delicious. A special recommendation: do try their Chicken Malai Tikka—it’s a must!

Overall rating: 8/10. If you’re a fan of Mughlai chicken, this restaurant is definitely worth a visit.

Chef, we wish you continued success and all the best for your future endeavours.

Thank you,
Sagar & Tejashree

featured_reviews.name: Akash Gogri
featured_reviews.review_text:
Paid premium price for a thoroughly mediocre experience, Eve was an absolute disappointment.

The staff seemed poorly trained and completely unprofessional, honestly felt like they had no hospitality background. The entire floor was chaotic, people shouting across sections, and managers constantly rearranging tables to squeeze in more guests. At one point, a table right next to us was given to new customers without even being cleaned.

Basic service etiquette was missing, plates weren’t changed unless we explicitly asked. On top of that, staff would hover right next to the table and the moment you finished a dish or drink, they’d immediately push you to order something else. It felt more like pressure than service.

Coming to the food, extremely underwhelming.
Nachos were the only decent dish. The mango salad had barely 7–8 pieces, the spaghetti was basic and poorly executed. Even classic cocktails like a Manhattan (served in the wrong glass!) and an Espresso Martini were messed up. Only the Picante managed to save some face.

Apart from the staircase with the “library” aesthetic, which is clearly designed for Instagram - there’s nothing special about this place.

For ~₹3,500 per person, this experience was nowhere close to worth it. There are far better restaurants in the city.

Avoid this place if you value your money and experience.

featured_reviews.name: sucheta thakur
featured_reviews.review_text:
Some restaurants get the ambiance right.
Some focus entirely on the food.
And then there are places like Megumi that manage to do both beautifully.

From the moment we walked in, the space felt warm, elegant, and calming without trying too hard. The kind of restaurant where you instantly know you’re going to enjoy spending time — whether it’s for a quiet dinner, a catch-up with friends, or simply a slow evening over good food.

The meal began with complimentary sweet potato chips served alongside a jalapeño dip and chilli oil, and honestly, this small opening already set the tone for the evening. Crisp, addictive, and paired with dips that added both heat and freshness — it was one of those thoughtful touches that immediately makes you feel taken care of.

We then moved on to the Daikon Cake, which was beautifully executed with a lovely balance of texture and flavour. Comforting, delicate, and packed with umami, it was the kind of dish that quietly impresses you.

The Spicy Corn Curd was another standout for me. Creamy, flavourful, and carrying just the right amount of spice, it struck that perfect balance between indulgent and light. Definitely one of those dishes I’d happily reorder.

But the real star of the meal was the Edamame and Truffle Fried Rice. Fragrant, comforting, and deeply satisfying, this dish had everything working in its favour. The truffle flavour was present without overpowering the dish, while the edamame added texture and freshness. Easily one of the best things we ate that evening.

We also tried the Smoked Cottage Cheese Robata, which brought in beautiful smoky flavours while still letting the softness of the cottage cheese shine through. Rich, well-balanced, and very satisfying.

To end the meal, we had the Almond Coffee Delicai, which was smooth, indulgent, and the perfect finish to the evening. The coffee and almond combination worked beautifully together without feeling too heavy.

Final thoughts:
Megumi delivers exactly what you hope for from a good Asian dining experience — thoughtful food, balanced flavours, warm hospitality, and an ambiance that makes you want to stay longer. Every dish felt carefully crafted, and the overall meal struck that lovely balance between comfort and elegance.

A beautiful dining experience in Santacruz that I’d happily go back to. ✨
